items.evidence: After page.reload() the spec checks the total again (diff line 101) and the Manual 25% row (line 103). Both values come from the server, so they would fail if the discount mutation never ran.

Each criterion has an assertion: the total at promoted price less 25% (lines 89 and 101), the Manual 25% row next to the Promotion row (lines 94-96), and the values still there after reload (lines 99-104).
The new members go on the existing DraftOrderPage and reuse its dialog, summary, discountToggle and total. No existing locator, helper or scenario constant is copied.
There are no fixed waits. The new method waits for the dialog to be hidden (line 42), and the spec uses web-first assertions.
The spec imports test and expect from fixtures/test.ts (line 54). It has no parallel() tag and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.

Elements are found by test ids (discount-value and discount-reason, which exist in DiscountFormFields.tsx) or by role and name, all scoped to the summary or the dialog. submit is scoped to the dialog (line 41).
The draft is started with DraftOrderPage.create and addProduct on top of ORDERS_SCENARIO. That is the suite's own pattern, and the spec makes no API calls.
Every expected amount is worked out from PRODUCTS.tee.price and PROMOTIONS. There are no hard-coded ids and no populatedb values.
The spec uses the default admin actor, which the ticket allows, and does not sign in through the UI or contain credentials.
typecheck.txt shows exit 0 with no errors. The file is at e2e/tests/orders/draft-manual-discount.spec.ts.
All locators and the multi-step discount action are on DraftOrderPage. The spec only calls page-object members and page.reload().
The new locators are readonly fields built from this.page, summary or dialog. The class keeps constructor(readonly page: Page) {}, and discountRow is a parameterised method like the existing ones.
The spec has // Arrange (line 72) and // Act & Assert (line 86).
It is one test with three test.step stages (lines 87, 93 and 99).
The title says what behaviour is checked and carries #e2e (line 69).
The header comment (lines 58-62) says what the spec covers and why.
Every assertion is web-first (toHaveText or toContainText on locators).
The spec uses ORDERS_SCENARIO, PRODUCTS, PROMOTIONS and CHANNEL, compares money with toFixed(2), and guards the arithmetic with expect(promotedSubtotal).toBeLessThan(...) (line 80).
There are no cleanup hooks and no unique or random names.
No timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState are added.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
There is no any, no cast and no gql call. The method parameters are typed.
The comments explain reasons: the arithmetic guard, why discountRow filters nested list items, and why the dialog opens from the expanded breakdown. None just restates the next line.
